newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Stoiber renews warnings against euro.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Stoiber renews warnings against euro.

text.p: Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber said on Friday the Maastricht criteria for Europe's single currency had to be fulfilled for the euro to be a credible currency for financial market and the public.

Stoiber, a leading figure in the Christian Social Union (CSU), told Bild newspaper that he was only interested in a stable currency and was not leading a campaign against the euro or against Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who has reportedly grown irritated at Stoiber's regular warnings about the euro.
"I am not leading an anti-euro debate and I am not leading an anti-chancellor debate, but rather a discussion about achieving a lastingly stable euro that is as strong as the mark," Stoiber said.
"The stability pact will only remain credible if the criteria and especially the limits on annual debt of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product are reached," Stoiber said.
"This is not a debate about decimal points, but rather a question of trust in a stable euro for the financial markets and public."
Bild added in the same article that, according to its sources, Stoiber was determined to vote against the euro in the Bundesrat if the Maastricht criteria are not fulfilled.
